current_strategy.rationale: Metformin is first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, effective for glycemic control and weight neutrality, with cardiovascular safety.

current_strategy.description: Continuation of metformin monotherapy given good tolerance and preserved renal function.
current_strategy.rationale: Metformin remains first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, especially with preserved renal function and good tolerance.
current_strategy.considerations: Monitor glycemic control and side effects; assess if HbA1c target <7% is achieved safely.

GLP-1_receptor_agonists.description: Consider GLP-1 receptor agonists as add-on therapy if glycemic targets are not met or for additional cardiovascular benefit.
GLP-1_receptor_agonists.rationale: GLP-1 RAs have demonstrated cardiovascular risk reduction in moderate to high risk patients and promote weight loss, which may benefit patients in the 80-99kg weight band.
GLP-1_receptor_agonists.considerations: Evaluate renal function, gastrointestinal tolerance, and patient preference before initiation.

SGLT2_inhibitors.description: Consider SGLT2 inhibitors for cardiovascular and renal protection, especially in moderate to high cardiovascular risk patients.
SGLT2_inhibitors.rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular events and have renal benefits; suitable if renal function is preserved or mildly reduced.
SGLT2_inhibitors.considerations: Monitor for volume depletion, genital infections, and renal function.

Other agents.description: DPP-4 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, or insulin may be considered based on glycemic control, hypoglycemia risk, and patient factors.
Other agents.rationale: Tailor therapy to individual needs, comorbidities, and risk profiles.

additional_agents.contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2.
